name: Stern Deck
hours: Open for the whole crossing. ARRIVAL DAY (Day 1, 08:00–10:40) on the stern: jessica — on the sheltered side beside three leather caskets stacked on a crewman's trolley, one gloved hand on the smallest; she does not leave them. She declines a game on a boat and before a proper introduction, and is glad of conversation with anyone who crossed the deck to offer it. ashton — at the rail near her with a rose, trying one line after another; he lost at the lounge table half an hour ago and says so cheerfully. He plays a casual game lazily, readily if a woman is watching, for no stake. victoria — on the one dry bench under the awning with a parasol open, looking at the wake; she does not play in a crowd. ophelia — a second-year, her sister, standing at the luggage cage with her arms crossed, watching the bench; she answers for Victoria when strangers crowd her and says 'after we dock' to any game. sunny — sitting on the lower bar of the rail with her bare feet over the wake and a towel round her neck; plays at once, on the planks, and proposes that the loser does ten push-ups. marit — standing on a mooring bollard reciting to the gulls, glad of a human audience; plays any game offered and narrates it for whoever gathers.
sight: The open after deck: a white wake running back to an empty horizon, gulls riding the air above the flagstaff, a wire luggage cage stacked to the top with trunks. One bench stands dry under a canvas awning; the rest of the planking shines with spray. It is quieter here than forward, the funnel is warm at your back, and the mainland is gone.
things: Watch the wake and the gulls
Stand at the rail with the wind behind you and say nothing to anybody
Cross the deck and introduce yourself to someone
Sit on the dry bench, if there is room and you ask
Play a casual game on the planks, cards under a shoe
Read the labels in the luggage cage and guess who owns what
Find your own duffel at the bottom of the cage
secret: No quarrel here by default: this is where the ship is calm, and where a player who wants to meet people rather than fight goes. Ashton's courtship of Jessica is going politely nowhere; she notices who crosses the deck to speak to her and how, and a plain greeting does more than a line. Victoria answers one person at a time, in complete sentences, if spoken to directly and plainly; a group or a joke gets silence, and then Ophelia. Sunny says what she likes about a person within a minute of meeting them. Marit's game draws a small crowd, which is hard on Rowan's hands. News travels aft: if Rowan has played at the lounge table, the stern knows the result before he arrives, and Ashton asks him how Gideon took it.
